about.title: Tulelake Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Tulelake is a small farming community in Siskiyou County, and residents here often travel some distance for specialized medical care — which means any breakdown in diagnosis, treatment, or follow-up can carry outsized consequences. If you or a family member suffered harm after a procedure, a missed diagnosis, or a medication mistake at a local clinic or a facility you were referred to, it's worth having someone review the records. California law, through MICRA, sets specific rules for these claims, including tight notice periods and a cap on certain damages. We handle medical negligence cases and can tell you, honestly, whether your situation looks like a case worth pursuing further. There's no obligation, and no cost unless we recover something for you.
commonInjuries: Delayed or missed diagnosis of a serious condition
Birth injuries to mother or newborn
Failure to monitor or follow up on abnormal test results

whyChoose.title: What Makes These Claims Different in California

items.title: Strict, Short Deadlines
items.desc: California generally gives you one year from when you discover the harm, and no more than three years from the injury itself, to bring a claim. Waiting to ask questions can quietly cost you your right to file.

items.title: A Notice Letter Comes First
items.desc: Before any lawsuit, California requires a 90-day notice to the provider or facility. We can make sure it's done correctly and on time.

items.title: Expert Review Is Almost Always Required
items.desc: A bad outcome by itself isn't proof of malpractice — California requires a qualified medical expert to weigh in on whether the care fell below the accepted standard. We can help arrange that kind of review.

items.question: I live in a small town like Tulelake — does that change how a malpractice claim works?
items.answer: The legal rules are the same statewide, but rural cases often involve care given at a facility outside Tulelake or Siskiyou County, since many residents travel for specialized treatment. We can still pursue the claim regardless of where the provider is located, as long as California law applies.

items.question: Is a bad medical outcome automatically malpractice?
items.answer: No. California law is clear that a poor result alone doesn't establish negligence. There has to be evidence that the provider's care fell below the accepted medical standard, which is why an expert review is typically required.

items.question: What does it cost to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: Nothing. Our team works on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no fee to ask questions or get an initial opinion.
